steps.body: Unplug the washer or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.

steps.title: Access machine electronics
steps.body: Remove the top panel. Visually verify all RFI filter and ACU connections are fully seated.

steps.title: RFI filter and ACU connections OK
steps.body: Are all interference filter and ACU harness connections secure and fully inserted?

steps.title: Restore power for voltage checks

steps.body: With AC voltmeter, measure line voltage at the interference filter input (power cord side).

measurements.title: Line voltage at RFI filter input

branches.label: No line voltage

steps.sourceExcerpt: With AC voltmeter, measure line voltage at the interference filter input (power cord side).

steps.title: Line voltage at RFI filter output
steps.body: Measure AC line voltage at the interference filter output toward the ACU.

testPoint.label: Line voltage at RFI filter output

measurements.title: Line voltage at RFI filter output

branches.oemOutcome: Replace the interference (RFI) filter.

branches.label: Out of range
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the interference (RFI) filter.

steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure AC line voltage at the interference filter output toward the ACU.

steps.title: AC input at ACU J2 pins 1 & 2

measurements.title: AC input at ACU J2 pins 1 & 2

branches.label: No voltage at J2

steps.title: ACU service LED healthy
steps.body: After power-up, does the ACU status LED blink slowly (0.5s on/off) within 30 seconds? (Not off, not rapid constant blink.)

branches.oemOutcome: Replace the ACU — microcontroller or 5 VDC supply fault indicated.

steps.sourceExcerpt: After power-up, does the ACU status LED blink slowly (0.5s on/off) within 30 seconds? (Not off, not rapid constant blink.)

branches.oemOutcome: Reconnect harnesses and repeat HMI test.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the washer or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing. Failure to do so can result in death or electrical shock. Replace all parts and panels before operating.

steps.title: Basket turns freely
steps.body: Manually check that the basket turns freely. Mechanical lockup must be resolved before electrical testing.

branches.label: Basket does not turn freely
branches.oemOutcome: Resolve mechanical friction or lockup before repeating motor circuit test.

steps.sourceExcerpt: Check to see if basket will turn freely. If basket does not turn freely, determine what is causing the mechanical friction or lockup.

steps.title: Access ACU and verify J6
steps.body: Remove the top to access the ACU. Perform TEST #1 ACU power check, then verify connector J6 is fully seated in the ACU. Disconnect the motor harness from the ACU before resistance checks.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove the top to access the ACU. Perform TEST #1: ACU Power Check, then visually check that connector J6 is inserted all the way into the ACU. Check the motor windings — disconnect the motor harness from the ACU.

steps.title: Motor windings J6 pins 1 & 2
steps.body: With an ohmmeter at the motor harness disconnected from the ACU, measure resistance between J6 pins 1 (Motor U, BU) and 2 (Motor V, W). Wire colors are at the stator harness (J36) per Figure 2.

branches.label: Outside range or open
branches.oemOutcome: Replace stator assembly.

branches.label: Open circuit (OL)
branches.oemOutcome: Replace stator assembly.

branches.label: Critical out of range
branches.oemOutcome: Replace stator assembly.

steps.sourceExcerpt: With an ohmmeter, verify the resistance values as shown: J6, Pins 1 & 2 — 6–20 Ω.

steps.title: Motor windings J6 pins 2 & 3
steps.body: Measure resistance between J6 pins 2 and 3.

branches.label: Outside range or open
branches.oemOutcome: Replace stator assembly.

branches.label: Open circuit (OL)
branches.oemOutcome: Replace stator assembly.

branches.label: Critical out of range
branches.oemOutcome: Replace stator assembly.

steps.title: Motor windings J6 pins 1 & 3
steps.body: Measure resistance between J6 pins 1 and 3.

branches.label: Outside range or open
branches.oemOutcome: Replace stator assembly.

branches.label: Open circuit (OL)
branches.oemOutcome: Replace stator assembly.

branches.label: Critical out of range
branches.oemOutcome: Replace stator assembly.

steps.sourceExcerpt: J6, Pins 1 & 3 — 6–20 Ω. If values are outside the range or open, replace stator assembly; otherwise reconnect the motor harness and go to step 7.

steps.title: Reconnect harness and restore power
steps.body: Reconnect the motor harness to the ACU. Reinstall panels as needed. Plug in or restore power. Door must be closed and locked before any motor test.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Plug in washer or reconnect power. IMPORTANT: Door must be closed and locked to run motor.

steps.title: Continue to Quick Service Cycle

steps.sourceExcerpt: Service Diagnostic mode must be active before Load Test / Quick Service Cycle.

branches.label: Motor not moving

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the washer or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing. Failure to do so can result in death or electrical shock.

steps.title: Door lock mechanism clear
steps.body: Check the door lock mechanism for obstruction or binding. Repair as needed before electrical testing.

branches.label: Obstruction or binding found
branches.oemOutcome: Clear obstruction or repair binding; then repeat TEST #4 from step 1.

steps.sourceExcerpt: Check door lock mechanism for obstruction or binding. Repair as necessary.

steps.title: Access ACU and verify J7
steps.body: Remove the top panel to access the ACU. Verify connector J7 (door lock assembly) is fully seated in the ACU.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove top panel to access machine electronics. Visually check that the J7 (door lock assembly) connector is inserted all the way into the ACU.

steps.title: J7 fully seated
steps.body: Is connector J7 fully inserted into the ACU?

branches.label: J7 loose or not seated
branches.oemOutcome: Reconnect J7 at the ACU, reassemble, restore power, and retest door lock with Quick Service Cycle.

steps.title: Energize door lock solenoid
steps.body: Disconnect J7 from the ACU. Restore power. Press POWER, select any cycle, and press START. Listen for the door lock solenoid to actuate (click) after a few seconds. Immediately unplug the washer, disconnect power, and leave J7 disconnected at the ACU for resistance checks.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Plug in washer or reconnect power. Press the POWER button, select any cycle, and then press START. Actuation of the door lock solenoid should be heard after a few seconds. At that point, unplug the washer and disconnect J7 from the ACU and measure resistance across pins (ACU side).

steps.title: Lock switch J7 pins 1 & 2
steps.body: With power disconnected and lock solenoid actuated, measure resistance between J7-1 and J7-2 at the ACU connector. Locked position should read 0 Ω (continuity).
steps.sourceExcerpt: Lock Switch — Locked = 0 ohms, Unlocked = Open Circuit — J7-1, J7-2.

steps.title: Door switch / solenoid J7 pins 2 & 3
steps.body: Measure resistance between J7-2 and J7-3 with the door closed and lock actuated. Expected 60–90 Ω.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Door Switch — Door Closed = 60-90 ohms — J7-2, J7-3. Lock Solenoid — 60-90 ohms with door closed — J7-2, J7-3.

steps.title: Check harness and door lock assembly
steps.body: Check harness continuity between the ACU and door lock mechanism. Verify connections at the door lock assembly. Remove door lock screws before removing the front panel when replacing the lock.
steps.sourceExcerpt: If any of the measurements are out of range, check the harness of the suspected component between the ACU and door lock mechanism for continuity. If the harness and connections are good, replace the door lock mechanism.

steps.title: Harness continuity OK
steps.body: Is there continuity through the harness between the ACU and door lock assembly?

branches.label: Harness continuity OK
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the door lock mechanism. Remove door lock screws before removing the front panel. Reassemble and verify with Quick Service Cycle.

branches.label: Harness open or damaged
branches.oemOutcome: Repair or replace harness between ACU and door lock; retest with Quick Service Cycle.

steps.title: Reconnect J7 and restore power
steps.body: Reinstall connector J7 on the ACU. Reassemble panels as needed. Plug in or restore power.

steps.title: Continue to Quick Service Cycle
steps.body: You should now be in Service Diagnostic mode. Continue below for Quick Service Cycle instructions.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Service Diagnostic mode must be active before Load Test / Quick Service Cycle.

steps.title: Door locks during Quick Service Cycle
steps.body: When starting Quick Service Cycle (function 012), does the door lock engage (click) and remain locked during the cycle?

branches.label: Door does not lock
branches.oemOutcome: Resistance values were in range but lock still fails — replace the ACU and retest door lock mechanism.

steps.sourceExcerpt: Check the relays and electrical connections to the door lock by performing the Quick Service Cycle. If door does not lock, see TEST #4.

branches.label: Obstruction or binding found
branches.oemOutcome: Clear obstruction or repair binding; then repeat TEST #4 from step 1.

branches.label: J7 loose or not seated
branches.oemOutcome: Reconnect J7 at the ACU, reassemble, restore power, and retest door lock with Quick Service Cycle.

branches.label: Harness continuity OK
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the door lock mechanism. Remove door lock screws before removing the front panel. Reassemble and verify with Quick Service Cycle.

branches.label: Harness open or damaged
branches.oemOutcome: Repair or replace harness between ACU and door lock; retest with Quick Service Cycle.

branches.label: Door does not lock
branches.oemOutcome: Resistance values were in range but lock still fails — replace the ACU and retest door lock mechanism.

steps.sourceExcerpt: Are J16 and drum light harness connections secure?

branches.label: 2.9–3.5 VDC
branches.oemOutcome: Replace drum LED — driver voltage present.

branches.label: Voltage not present
branches.oemOutcome: Replace ACU — drum light driver fault.

steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure VDC across J16 pins 1 and 3 with drum light disconnected. Expected 2.9–3.5 VDC.

steps.title: Live valve test failed
steps.body: This procedure continues after Quick Service Cycle / load test did not activate the suspect valve.
steps.sourceExcerpt: This procedure continues after Quick Service Cycle / load test did not activate the suspect valve.

steps.title: Disconnect J8 at ACU
steps.body: Remove top panel. Disconnect connector J8. Verify harness continuity to valve coils.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove top panel. Disconnect connector J8. Verify harness continuity to valve coils.

steps.title: Inlet valve coil resistance
steps.body: Measure coil resistance: C1 J8-1&2, C2 J8-1&3, Hot J8-1&5. Expected 1.1–1.35 kΩ each.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Measure coil resistance: C1 J8-1&2, C2 J8-1&3, Hot J8-1&5. Expected 1.1–1.35 kΩ each.

steps.sourceExcerpt: Reconnect J8 to ACU. Restore power for live activation test via QSC/load test.

steps.title: Valve energizes with line voltage

branches.label: No line voltage at valve
branches.oemOutcome: Replace ACU — no drive voltage to valve.

steps.sourceExcerpt: During load test or component activation, does the suspect valve receive line voltage and open?

branches.oemOutcome: Replace ACU — no drive voltage to valve.

branches.label: Hose/trap issue
branches.oemOutcome: Clear hose/air trap, repair routing, replace leaking hose; retest fill.

steps.sourceExcerpt: Are tub-to-trap, trap-to-hose, and hose-to-APS connections secure with no kinks, leaks, or debris?

steps.title: Verify J14 at ACU
steps.body: Remove top/rear access as needed. Verify J14 fully seated and APS harness connected.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove top/rear access as needed. Verify J14 fully seated and APS harness connected.

steps.title: Harness continuity ACU to APS

branches.label: Open harness
branches.oemOutcome: Repair or replace harness between ACU and APS.

steps.sourceExcerpt: Is there continuity in the harness between ACU J14 and the water level sensor?

steps.sourceExcerpt: Plug in washer for DC measurement at J14.

steps.body: Black probe to J14 pin 2 (GND), red to pin 3. Expect +5 VDC.

testPoint.label: +5 VDC at J14 (pin 2 GND, pin 3 Vcc)

measurements.title: +5 VDC at J14 (pin 2 GND, pin 3 Vcc)

branches.oemOutcome: Drain tub, replace water level sensor (APS).

branches.label: +5 VDC missing
branches.oemOutcome: Perform TEST #1 ACU Power Check; replace ACU if supply fault persists.

steps.sourceExcerpt: Black probe to J14 pin 2 (GND), red to pin 3. Expect +5 VDC.

testPoint.label: +5 VDC at J14 (pin 2 GND, pin 3 Vcc)

measurements.title: +5 VDC at J14 (pin 2 GND, pin 3 Vcc)

branches.label: Hose/trap issue

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the washer or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing. Failure to do so can result in death or electrical shock. Replace all parts and panels before operating.

steps.title: Obstructions cleared
steps.body: Check the drain pump filter, drain hose, and usual blockage areas. Clean as needed before electrical testing.

branches.label: Obstruction found or not yet cleared
branches.oemOutcome: Clear obstructions in the drain filter, hose, and pump area; then repeat TEST #8 from step 1.

steps.sourceExcerpt: Check for obstructions in the usual areas. Clean and then perform step 2. Check the Drain Pump/Recirculation Pump filter for foreign objects.

steps.title: Access ACU and verify J11
steps.body: Remove the top panel to access the ACU. Perform TEST #1 ACU power check if needed. Verify connector J11 is fully seated in the ACU before resistance checks.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove top panel to access machine electronics. Visually check that the J11 connector is inserted all the way into the ACU. If connector is not inserted properly, reconnect J11 and repeat Quick Service Cycle step 004.

steps.title: J11 fully seated
steps.body: Is connector J11 fully inserted into the ACU?

branches.label: J11 loose or not seated
branches.oemOutcome: Reconnect J11 at the ACU, reassemble, restore power, and repeat Quick Service Cycle step 004 (Drain Pump).

steps.title: Drain pump J11 pins 1 & 2
steps.body: Remove connector J11 from the ACU. Measure resistance between J11-1 (Drain Pump) and J11-2 (LINE_MR) at room temperature.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove connector J11 from the ACU. With an ohmmeter, measure the resistance across connector pins. Drain Pump — J11-1 to J11-2 — 18.5–21.5 Ω.

steps.title: Recirc pump J11 pins 3 & 4 (optional)
steps.body: At the same J11 connector, measure between J11-3 (Recirc pump L) and J11-4 (Recirc pump N). Expected 36–46 Ω at room temperature.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Recirculation Pump — J11-3 to J11-4 — 36–46 Ω.

steps.title: Inspect pump, hoses, and harness
steps.body: Open the bulk drawer and remove the pump filter cap. Remove bulk drawer, front panel, and backer as needed. Verify pump, filter, drain hose, recirculation hose/nozzle, and pressure switch hose are free of obstructions. Check electrical connections at the drain and recirculation pumps.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Open bulk drawer and remove pump filter cap. Verify that pump, pump filter, drain hose, recirculation hose/nozzle, and pressure switch hose are free from obstructions. Visually check the electrical connections at the Drain Pump and Recirculation Pumps.

steps.title: Pump connections secure
steps.body: Are pump electrical connections tight and hoses free of blockage?

branches.label: Loose connections found
branches.oemOutcome: Reconnect pump electrical connections, reassemble, restore power, and repeat Quick Service Cycle step 004.

steps.title: Harness continuity to ACU
steps.body: With an ohmmeter, is there continuity between the drain/recirc pump and the ACU on the lower machine harness?

branches.label: No continuity
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the lower machine harness, reassemble, restore power, and repeat Quick Service Cycle.

steps.sourceExcerpt: With an ohmmeter, check harness for continuity between the Drain Pump/Recirculation Pump and ACU. If there is no continuity, replace the lower machine harness and repeat step 2.

steps.title: Drain pump ohms at pump terminals
steps.body: Measure resistance across the two drain pump terminals using the same 18.5–21.5 Ω specification.

measurements.title: Drain pump ohms at pump terminals

branches.label: Open (OL)
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the drain pump assembly. Reassemble, restore power, and run Quick Service Cycle step 004 to verify.

branches.label: Outside range
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the drain pump assembly.

branches.label: Critical out of range
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the drain pump assembly.

branches.label: 18.5–21.5 Ω at pump
branches.oemOutcome: Pump windings and harness test good at the pump — replace the ACU if drain still fails.

steps.sourceExcerpt: With an ohmmeter, measure the resistance across the two pump terminals using the chart in step 6. If the reading is infinite (open), replace the drain pump assembly.

steps.title: Reconnect J11 and restore power
steps.body: Reinstall connector J11 on the ACU. Reassemble panels as needed. Plug in or restore power.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Replace all parts and panels before operating.

steps.title: Continue to Quick Service Cycle
steps.body: You should now be in Service Diagnostic mode. Continue below for Quick Service Cycle instructions.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Service Diagnostic mode must be active before Load Test / Quick Service Cycle.

steps.title: Drain pump runs during QSC step 004
steps.body: During Quick Service Cycle function 004 (Drain Pump), does the drain pump turn on and run?

branches.label: Drain pump does not run
branches.oemOutcome: Windings test in range but pump did not run in service mode — inspect wiring, harness, and ACU output; replace ACU if outputs are missing.

steps.sourceExcerpt: 004 — Drain Pump — Turns on the drain pump. If drain pump does not turn on, see TEST #8: Drain/Recirculation Pump.

measurements.title: Drain pump ohms at pump terminals

branches.label: Obstruction found or not yet cleared
branches.oemOutcome: Clear obstructions in the drain filter, hose, and pump area; then repeat TEST #8 from step 1.

branches.label: J11 loose or not seated
branches.oemOutcome: Reconnect J11 at the ACU, reassemble, restore power, and repeat Quick Service Cycle step 004 (Drain Pump).

branches.label: Loose connections found
branches.oemOutcome: Reconnect pump electrical connections, reassemble, restore power, and repeat Quick Service Cycle step 004.

branches.label: No continuity
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the lower machine harness, reassemble, restore power, and repeat Quick Service Cycle.

branches.label: Open (OL)
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the drain pump assembly. Reassemble, restore power, and run Quick Service Cycle step 004 to verify.

branches.label: Outside range
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the drain pump assembly.

branches.label: Critical out of range
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the drain pump assembly.

branches.label: 18.5–21.5 Ω at pump
branches.oemOutcome: Pump windings and harness test good at the pump — replace the ACU if drain still fails.

branches.label: Drain pump does not run
branches.oemOutcome: Windings test in range but pump did not run in service mode — inspect wiring, harness, and ACU output; replace ACU if outputs are missing.

steps.title: Disconnect power
steps.body: Unplug the washer or disconnect power before servicing. Replace all parts and panels before operating.
steps.sourceExcerpt: WARNING — Electrical Shock Hazard. Disconnect power before servicing. Failure to do so can result in death or electrical shock.

steps.title: Access ACU and disconnect J3
steps.body: Remove the top panel to access the ACU. Disconnect connector J3 (wash heater) from the ACU.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove top panel to access machine electronics. Disconnect connector J3 from the ACU.

steps.title: Wash heater J3 pins 1 & 2
steps.body: With J3 disconnected at the ACU, measure resistance across pins 1 and 2. Expected 7–30 Ω at room temperature.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Using an ohmmeter, measure the resistance across pins 1 and 2 of connector J3. If the resistance is 7-30 Ω, the heating element and wiring are good.

steps.title: Access heating element
steps.body: Remove the back panel to access the heating element. Disconnect the wire connectors from the heating element terminals.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Remove back panel to access the heating element. Disconnect the wire connectors from the heating element.

steps.title: Heater ohms at element terminals
steps.body: Measure resistance across the two heating element terminals. Expected 7–30 Ω.

branches.label: Open circuit (OL)
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the heating element. Torque heater nut to 4.5 Nm ± 0.5 Nm on reinstall. Verify drum clearance after install.

branches.label: Outside 7–30 Ω
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the heating element.

branches.label: Critical out of range
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the heating element.

branches.label: 7–30 Ω at element
branches.oemOutcome: Heating element is good — replace the lower main harness and retest with Quick Service Cycle.

steps.sourceExcerpt: Using an ohmmeter, measure the resistance across the two heating element terminals. If the resistance is open, replace the heating element. If 7-30 Ω, replace the lower main harness.

steps.title: Reconnect J3 and restore power
steps.body: Reinstall connector J3 on the ACU. Reassemble panels as needed. Plug in or restore power.

steps.title: Continue to Quick Service Cycle
steps.body: You should now be in Service Diagnostic mode. Continue below for Quick Service Cycle instructions.
steps.sourceExcerpt: Service Diagnostic mode must be active before Load Test / Quick Service Cycle.

steps.title: Heater energizes during QSC step 008
steps.body: During Quick Service Cycle function 008 (Heater), does the wash heater turn on (tub warms / heater relay engages)?

branches.label: Heater does not energize
branches.oemOutcome: Resistance was in range but heater did not energize — replace the ACU and retest with Quick Service Cycle.

steps.sourceExcerpt: 008 — Heater — Adds cold water to the drum, turns on heater. If heater does not turn on, see TEST #9: Wash Heating Element.

branches.label: Open circuit (OL)
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the heating element. Torque heater nut to 4.5 Nm ± 0.5 Nm on reinstall. Verify drum clearance after install.

branches.label: Outside 7–30 Ω
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the heating element.

branches.label: Critical out of range
branches.oemOutcome: Replace the heating element.

branches.label: 7–30 Ω at element
branches.oemOutcome: Heating element is good — replace the lower main harness and retest with Quick Service Cycle.

branches.label: Heater does not energize
branches.oemOutcome: Resistance was in range but heater did not energize — replace the ACU and retest with Quick Service Cycle.
